sentences.text: Now the walls.
Many potentials draw the same {b}field{/}: add the slope of any hill, and the curl is unchanged.
Choose among them without a fixed rule, and the {model}generator{/} learns noise.
So fix the gauge: no divergence inside, no potential flowing through the wall.
A published theorem then gives each admissible {b}field{/} one potential: none lost, none counted twice.
If the {b}field{/} never crosses the wall, the potential may instead meet it at right angles.
One {metric}metric{/} changes meaning: where the {b}field{/} crosses the wall, magnetic helicity depends on the gauge, so a relative helicity is needed.

sentences.text: Now the iron that made VKS work.
At its surface, the part of the {b}field{/} crossing it is continuous, and so is the part along it, divided by the permeability.
Can a smooth potential obey both rules?
No: a smooth potential keeps the {b}field{/} continuous, breaking the second rule unless the {b}field{/} meets the iron head-on.
The plan proposes an untested fix: a potential deliberately kinked at the surface.
Outside, the {b}field{/} must join a current-free field: linear but nonlocal, each wall point depending on the whole wall.
How to impose it is open.

sentences.text: In the periodic box, two scalars, poloidal and toroidal, can replace a potential's three components.
Their {b}field{/} is divergence-free, with no gauge: the plan stores its box data that way.
The partners' solver slices space instead: around the axis, waves of zero, one, two, three bumps per turn; across each half-plane, a triangle mesh.
A continuous potential on that mesh gives a divergence-free curl, wave by wave.
But the solver's data are only nearly divergence-free: the {model}generator{/} will be cleaner than its data.
Measure with the solver's yardstick.

question.fr: Quelles étiquettes chaque instantané VKS doit-il porter : quelle *définition de Rm*, quelle *condition de paroi*, quelle perméabilité du fer ?
question.why: A generator learns whatever its labels mean: one VKS threshold reads 31 or 52–71 depending on the Rm definition, and the wall condition alone moves a simulated threshold by about 40 %.
question.unblocks: Framing of tier 3: the conditioning vector (Re, Rm in one stated convention, μ_r, forcing asymmetry, wall condition, impeller phase) and the metadata each converted snapshot carries; hence which μ_r and wall-condition runs to request.
question.why_fr: Un générateur apprend ce que signifient ses étiquettes : un même seuil VKS vaut 31 ou 52–71 selon la définition de Rm, et la seule condition de paroi déplace un seuil simulé d'environ 40 %.
question.unblocks_fr: Cadrage du palier 3 : le vecteur de conditionnement (Re, Rm dans une convention annoncée, μ_r, asymétrie de forçage, condition de paroi, phase des turbines) et les métadonnées de chaque instantané converti ; donc quelles simulations en μ_r et en condition de paroi demander.
